clue.text: Hazards as revolutionary's taken over party in Africa

indicators.note: a party taken over by someone sits within that person's grip, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary; with the possessive he gives CHE'S
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Political hazards when a revolutionary seizes control of an African party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards and chances are both risks or gambles one takes.

clue.text: Cold partner liable to take up quite a lot of the bed?

definitions.text: liable to take up quite a lot of the bed?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
hubby is informal for husband

explanation.surface: A chilly husband who hogs the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone plump takes up more room, so a portly sleeper would fill much of the bed.

clue.text: A change one introduced — it has some flapping

indicators.note: introduced means brought into, so the numeral goes inside the word for change

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A change is made, one brought in, which causes flapping and fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A large enclosure for birds is full of flapping wings.

clue.text: A pose is struck with operators of intelligence embracing such stars

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the agency's letters surround the rearranged letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: struck here means knocked about, so these three words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Intelligence officers strike a pose with stars of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pose is struck' reads as a model posing, but 'struck' is the anagram signal, making SIOPEIA for 'embracing' to place inside the agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A W-shaped northern constellation named after a vain queen of Greek myth.

clue.text: The ultimate in treats for good child

indicators.note: the ultimate is the last, so take the final letter of treats

parts.note: pro means in favour of, or for

explanation.surface: The best of treats for a well-behaved child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child or baby.

clue.text: Wild flower masking end of garden

indicators.note: to mask something is to cover it up, so the flower surrounds the other letter

parts.note: the violet is a small purple flower

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: A wild flower growing over the far end of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: wild behaviour is violent, unrestrained and savage.

clue.text: Very silly person, aged prisoner being held in form of subjection

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: being held in tells us the prisoner sits inside the abbreviation for aged

parts.note: ae. is the abbreviation of Latin aetatis, meaning aged, seen on tombstones
an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A foolish old prisoner kept in some form of servitude.
explanation.walkthrough: AE, short for Latin aetatis, means 'aged' and is often seen on old memorials.
explanation.definitionFit: The feudal state of a vassal, a dependant owing service to a lord, is a form of subjection.

clue.text: Form of therapy is provided by someone to give us a lift

definitions.text: someone to give us a lift

parts.note: OT is occupational therapy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Therapy is offered by someone who lifts our spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Otis is the famous American elevator company, named after its founder Elisha Otis.
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha Otis pioneered the safety elevator; his firm's lifts carry people upwards.

clue.text: Once a person who would dig below the surface as questioner?

parts.note: ex means former, once

parts.words: person who would dig below the surface
parts.note: a miner digs underground

explanation.surface: A former investigator who digs deep into matters by asking questions.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner tests candidates by setting questions.

clue.text: Opportunity to remember tabloid's decline

parts.note: a decline is a going down
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; the possessive gives 'of the Sun'

explanation.surface: A chance to recall the downfall of a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Binyon's 'For the Fallen', recited on Remembrance Day: 'At the going down of the sun and in the morning, We will remember them.'
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's line names sunset as the moment the fallen are remembered.

clue.text: Fool in America offering dollars and cents, say

indicators.note: in places the fool inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the United States
a nit is a silly person, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A fool in America offering money in dollars and cents.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollars and cents are examples of units of currency, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Suspend curate — it's for being unorthodox

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A bishop suspends a curate for heterodox views.
explanation.walkthrough: To rusticate, in British universities, is to send a student away for a time as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusticate is the Oxbridge term for temporarily expelling, or suspending, a student.

clue.text: Like 12 out in 20 at 12?

parts.note: 12 is a dog's name and 20 is the sun, so this is a dog out in the midday sun, as in Noel Coward's song 'Mad Dogs and Englishmen'

explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward's song says only mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun; a dog that does is mad, and dogs bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy, with a pun on a dog's bark, describing the hound of the Coward song out at noon.

clue.text: Fine personal commitment that may help clear the air

definitions.text: that may help clear the air

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
'I do' is the vow each partner makes at a wedding

explanation.surface: A fine personal pledge that might clear the air between people.
explanation.walkthrough: FIDO was the wartime Fog Investigation and Dispersal Operation, burning fuel beside runways to clear fog; it is also a stock name for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime system burnt petrol along airfields to disperse fog, literally clearing the air for aircraft.

clue.text: Painter has bit to put right around one room

indicators.note: putting something right around means reordering it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a cell is a small room
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A painter has a bit of tidying to do around a single room.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandro Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance painter of The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: Philosopher's theory pagan slammed

indicators.note: something slammed is knocked about violently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher's theory is slammed as pagan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher's theory' reads as one phrase; the definition is just 'Philosopher's', an adjective meaning of Pythagoras.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the Greek philosopher Pythagoras, as in his theorem.

clue.text: Knack for raising fish under river — it becomes a battle

indicators.note: in a down clue the fish goes under, after, the river
raising means lifting up, which in a down clue reads the word backwards

parts.note: an art is a knack or skill
the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A knack for landing fish beneath a river becomes a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson's 1805 naval victory off Cape Trafalgar is one of Britain's most famous battles.

clue.text: Flowery bits girl used to fill gaps

indicators.note: something used to fill a gap goes inside it, so the girl goes into the gaps

parts.note: spaces are gaps
Di is a short girl's name, for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl used to fill gaps with bits of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadix is a fleshy flower spike, as in arum lilies; these are the plural.

clue.text: Hard man or woman, one beginning to climb up monument

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the whole string is reversed

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Pat can be short for Patrick or Patricia
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word climb

explanation.surface: A tough person, starting to climb up a monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial to the dead buried elsewhere, like London's in Whitehall.

clue.text: Last word in forecast creates quandary

indicators.note: in tells us the last word sits inside the forecast

parts.note: to forecast is to predict
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: The final word in a weather forecast creates a dilemma.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a quandary is a difficult situation with no clear way out.

clue.text: See 8
See 8
Bad temper about catastrophe

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for bad temper is read backwards

parts.note: to be in a mood is to be sulky or bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper over a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a catastrophe is a terrible fate or ruin.

clue.text: On-board protection

parts.note: suggests protection aboard a ship, but the board is a dining table and the protection covers it

explanation.walkthrough: Board is an old word for a table, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth laid over a table protects its surface from spills during meals.

clue.text: Deposit diminished in value, nothing saved

indicators.note: something saved is kept within, so the zero sits inside

parts.note: less means smaller in value
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bank deposit losing value, with nothing saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine wind-blown soil laid down as a geological deposit.

clue.text: Stone ring with china buried below it

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece buried below another comes after it

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
china, from rhyming slang china plate, means mate or pal

explanation.surface: A stone ring with porcelain set beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a gemstone, a precious stone set in rings.

clue.text: Winner, short girl — sparkling type

parts.note: a champ is a champion, a winner

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Agnes is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A winning, short girl described as a sparkling type of person.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known sparkling wine, from the Champagne region of France.

clue.text: Products from Marks?

parts.note: Marks & Spencer is a British department store whose ranges of goods are product ...; ... are also marks drawn with a pen

explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer, known as Marks, is a British high-street store; shops sell product lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's ranges of goods are its product lines, and lines are also the strokes made by a pen.

clue.text: Description of panel admitting child as pupil

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so the panel's word takes in the child

parts.note: a solar panel is a kind of panel, so solar describes one

explanation.surface: An interview panel admitting a child as a pupil to the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a scholar is a student, especially one at school or on a scholarship.

clue.text: Get tense, if female carries gun around

indicators.note: one who carries something holds it within, so the gun goes round the letters
around confirms the gun is wrapped about the other letters

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone tensing up when a woman carries a gun about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to stiffen is to grow rigid or taut, as muscles do under strain.
